text: Now you, speak the things that suit sound doctrine:
older men are to be sober, dignified, prudent, sound in the faith, in love and in endurance;
similarly older women are to be reverent in behavior, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of what is good
—so that they may instruct the young women to love their husbands, to love their children,
to be prudent, pure, homemakers, good, Or, ‘good homemakers’. subordinating themselves to their own husbands, so that the Word of God not be maligned.
Similarly, exhort the young men to be self-controlled, Curiously the young men get only one requirement—self-control.

in all things presenting yourself as an example of good works: Again, if we are going to represent God in an official capacity, we need to be clean. showing integrity, dignity and incorruptibility in your teaching

—healthy speech, beyond reproach—so that the opponent may be put to shame, having nothing slighting to say about us. A significant minority of the Greek manuscripts have ‘you’ (as in AV and NKJV), but the majority (including the best line of transmission) has ‘us’. Since Titus’ message and authority derive from Paul, it is properly first person.
Exhort slaves to subordinate themselves to their own owners, to be well pleasing in all things, not talking back,

not pilfering but showing total trustworthiness, so as to adorn the doctrine of our Savior God in everything. Notice that Paul does not incite slaves to revolt or rebellion. Perhaps it is especially in adverse circumstances that we can ‘adorn’ the doctrine of God.
For the saving grace of God has appeared for all men,

teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live prudently, righteously and godly in this present age, God’s saving grace has been made available for every one, but most people haven’t heard of it. If they are to hear, we must live godly lives.

looking for the blessed hope, If we are to live ‘looking’, then we regard it as something that could happen in our lifetime (otherwise there’s no point in ‘looking’). even the glorious appearing of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,

who gave Himself for us, so that He might redeem us from all lawlessness Since any ‘law’ that God promulgates derives from His character, I take the point here to be that God wants to deliver us from anything and everything that is not in conformity to His character. and purify for Himself a special people, zealous for good works. There is repeated emphasis on doing what is good, not just professing correct doctrine.
Speak these things, whether you exhort or reprove, with all authority. Let no one disdain you. The problem here could be his youth, but as Paul’s delegate he represents apostolic authority.
